chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Khash’amy, who said:

Hafs Al-Kunany asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was in his presence, about the Words of Allah (Exalted and Majestic): 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to undertake the journey to it.'

He said: 'What is meant by that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who is sound in his body, his flock being tended to for him, has provisions and a mount, so he is from those who have the capacity for Hajj,' or he said: 'From those who have wealth for him.'

So Hafs Al-Kunany said to him: 'So when he is sound in his body, his flock being tended to for him, has provisions and a mount, and he does not perform Hajj, is he from those who have the capacity for Hajj?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.مَنِ اسْتَطاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا: Whoever is able to undertake the journey to it
key_terms.مُخَلًّى سَرْبُهُ: His flock/herd being tended to/cared for

ai.seo_question: What constitutes the legal definition of 'ability' (istita'ah) for the obligation of Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential definition of 'istita'ah' (ability) for Hajj, emphasizing that it requires not only physical health but also financial sufficiency and the care of dependents. It highlights the practical implication that mere capability without action confirms the obligation, a key point in distinguishing between the condition of ability and the act of performance. The hadith reflects the Imams' detailed approach to linking Quranic verses with specific socio-economic realities of the time.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Khash’amy who said,

‘Hafs Al-Kunany asked Abu Abdullahasws, and I was in hisasws presence, about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:97] and Hajj to the House is incumbent upon the people for the Sake of Allah, (upon) every one who is able to undertake the journey to it, what is Meant by that?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘The one who was of well-being in his body, his flock having been freed (looked after) for him, provisions, and ride, so he is from the ones who has the capacity for the Hajj’, or said: ‘From the ones who has wealth for him’.

So Hafs Al-Kinany said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So when he was of well-being in his body, his flock having been freed (looked after) for him, provisions, and ride, so he is from the ones who has the capacity for the Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath’amiy who has said the following:

“Hafs al-Kunasiy once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘It is obligatory upon people from Allah to perform al-Hajj who have the way (are able) to do so.’ [3:96]

He (the Imam) said, ‘It means that one is physically safe, has supplies and transportation, then he has the way (is able) to perform al-Hajj or that he (the Imam) said that he is of the ones who is wealthy.’

Hafs al-Kunasiy then asked, ‘So if one is physically safe, free, has supplies, transportation and has not performed al-Hajj, is he of those who are able to perform al- Hajj? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, that is correct.’”
